claim_being_audited: Whether certifying the model for launch is policy-compliant and evidentially supported despite a known below-target cybersecurity alert triage weakness remaining exposed in the initial rollout.

concern_ledger.concern: No admissible evidence shows the required pre-launch disclosure was made for the cybersecurity alert triage limitation.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Final model card or equivalent launch disclosure explicitly covering the limitation for the affected use case.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: The policy requires disclosure for material limitations affecting named launch use cases unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.

concern_ledger.concern: The affected cybersecurity alert triage segment remains eligible in the initial rollout cohort.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Evidence that the rollout gate excludes the affected segment or that launch scope was narrowed before launch.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: The policy says rollout controls mitigate only if they exclude the affected use case or are paired with approved risk acceptance.

concern_ledger.concern: The only risk acceptance record is an unapproved draft that does not mention the specific exposed weakness.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Approved risk acceptance signed before launch that specifically addresses cybersecurity alert triage exposure and rationale.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: Unapproved and nonspecific risk acceptance does not satisfy the policy exception.

decision_criteria: Under the policy, material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Rollout controls and post-launch monitoring mitigate the weakness only if they exclude the affected use case or are paired with reviewed risk acceptance explaining acceptable exposure.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents are relevant but not sufficient when a material use-case-specific limitation remains exposed.
A compliant certification requires admissible evidence for the governing policy predicate, not only operational prudence or public governance guidance.
evidence_requests: Provide the final pre-launch model card or equivalent disclosure showing the cybersecurity alert triage limitation was explicitly disclosed for the named launch use case.
Provide an approved risk acceptance record, signed before launch, that specifically addresses the exposed cybersecurity alert triage weakness and explains why exposure is acceptable.
Provide evidence that the initial rollout cohort was modified to exclude the affected cybersecurity alert triage segment, if that is being asserted.
Provide the formal certification record showing how the policy exception was satisfied.
specific_concerns: The affected cybersecurity alert triage use case remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort while below target on lateral-movement alert summarization.
The rollout controls are insufficient under the stated policy because the gate is random by tenant and does not exclude the affected use case.
The only risk acceptance evidence is an unapproved draft with a blank approver line, and it does not address the specific exposed cybersecurity alert triage weakness.
There is no admissible evidence that the required model-card disclosure for this named launch use case was completed before launch.

Aggregate readiness and reversible rollout controls do not satisfy the policy predicate that requires either exclusion of the affected use case or approved risk acceptance explaining why exposure is acceptable.
unsupported_claims: The recommendation to certify the model is not supported by admissible evidence as a compliant certification decision.
Any implication that rollout monitoring, rollback capability, or a 9% launch percentage cures the disclosure obligation is unsupported under the stated policy.
Any implication that the risk acceptance draft covers the exposed cybersecurity alert triage limitation is unsupported by the draft evidence.
